This document is both a working example and a guided tour.
Its suggestions, comments and replies are real review annotations rendered by the extension.
The study, people and results below are fictional.

[Download the Word example](index.docx) · [Download the editable example](downloads/walkthrough.zip) · [View the project on GitHub](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review)

## Start with the controls

Use the **Review** controls above to explore this manuscript.
These controls stay available as you scroll.

1. Switch **Text view** between **Redline**, **Original** and **Proposed** to compare pending wording.
2. Hover over a marked passage, select its comment label, or use **Next comment** to read the discussion beside the text.
3. Choose **Reading view** to hide controls, comments and markup; **Show review** brings them back.

On narrow screens, comments appear next to their passages in the document flow.
The page is a read-only review: changing a view or filter does not accept an edit or change anyone's comments.
The final section shows how to make and save those changes locally.

## Compare suggested wording

The study found [a {~~large~>modest~~}{#s1 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:00:00Z} difference in recall]{#c1}.
Participants remembered more words after spaced practice{++ than after massed practice++}{#s2 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:05:00Z}.
The result was {--very --}{#s3 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:10:00Z}consistent across the two lists.

**Try it:** switch to **Original**, then **Proposed**.
The replacement, insertion and deletion above are pending, so all three respond to that choice.
The comment on the first sentence explains the replacement and includes a reply.

To propose a replacement in the source, use CriticMarkup with a stable ID and an author alias:

~~~markdown
The study found a {~~large~>modest~~}{#s1 by=R} difference in recall.
~~~

The review.authors mapping in the document's front matter defines each alias once.
Names and dates remain attached to individual suggestions and messages.

## Follow comments and replies

Participants completed []{#c2-start}two practice sessions []{#c3-start}one week apart[]{#c2-end}, followed by a delayed recall test[]{#c3-end}.
The [recruitment target was 40 participants]{#c4}.

**Try it:** inspect the two overlapping comments on the first sentence.
One asks about the sessions; the other asks about timing.
Each retains its own passage even though the ranges overlap.
Robin's thread also includes a reply to Alex's reply.

The recruitment comment is already **resolved**.
Use the **Status** filter to find resolved discussions, then return to **All statuses**.
Use **Author** to focus on a reviewer; threads also match their reply participants.
**Hide comments** and **Hide controls** work independently.

For an ordinary comment, put a short range marker in the prose and its discussion elsewhere in the same QMD file:

~~~markdown
The [recruitment target was 40 participants]{#c4}.

:::: {.review-thread #c4 by=M .resolved}
Is this the planned or final sample?

::: {.reply #r4 by=A}
The planned sample; I have made that explicit.
:::
::::
~~~

Moving the discussion block does not move the comment's anchor.
Overlapping comments use explicit start and end markers, as demonstrated in the downloadable source.

## See ordinary edits too

Participants completed a five-minute practice session before the task.

This sentence was edited directly in index.qmd without adding CriticMarkup.
The frozen reference.qmd still says, “Participants completed a short practice session.”
Their comparison supplies the visible suggestion automatically.
Try the two text views to inspect that difference.

Keep editing index.qmd during a review round and leave reference.qmd frozen.
Changes to replies or comment status do not create manuscript wording changes.
To give an automatically detected edit a persistent decision, use its ID from the feedback command; the extension records it explicitly in the source.

## Recognise decisions already made

The task was {~~hard~>demanding~~}{#s4 by=R .accepted}.
The finding {~~suggests~>proves~~}{#s5 by=M .rejected} that spacing may improve recall.

The first suggestion was **accepted**; the second was **rejected**.
Both text views therefore show “demanding” and “suggests”.
The alternatives and their attribution remain in the source for review history.
The **Full review index** at the end of the page lists suggestions and their current decisions.

Comment resolution and suggestion acceptance are separate actions.
Resolving a discussion does not accept a nearby wording change.
Reopening it brings the discussion back without undoing text decisions.

## Keep feedback readable

[The reporting checklist includes the estimate, its uncertainty and the sample size]{#c5}.
A colleague also asked us to [retain a literal notation example]{#c6}.

The checklist comment demonstrates **emphasis**, a list, a link and inline code inside a discussion.
The notation comment demonstrates plain text: its asterisks and brackets are deliberately literal.
Imported Word comments retain that literal interpretation by default, so formatting characters do not silently change their meaning.

This example uses Quarto's standard manuscript layout.
Layout and output formats still belong in the project's _quarto.yml; review controls sit alongside them.
Installed manuscript formats, including APAQuarto, can be selected there.

## Work on your own copy {#work-locally}

Download and unzip the [editable example](downloads/walkthrough.zip).
It contains the working index.qmd, frozen reference.qmd, presentation settings and a short setup guide.
With Quarto and Python 3.12 or later installed, run these commands from that folder:

~~~sh
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review.git
quarto-review enable
quarto preview index.qmd --to html
~~~

On Windows, activate the environment with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in PowerShell.
Change the QMD and let the HTML preview refresh while you work.
You can also use the review commands:

~~~sh
quarto-review feedback --id c1
quarto-review reply c1 --body "I agree with the revised description."
quarto-review resolve c1
quarto-review reopen c1
quarto-review accept s1
quarto-review reject s2
~~~

Each command updates the working QMD while leaving the reference frozen.
The delete-comment command removes a whole discussion and its range markers while preserving the manuscript wording.
Use it only when you mean to remove the discussion.

When ready to share a Word draft, render it explicitly:

~~~sh
quarto render index.qmd --to docx
~~~

The [Word example](index.docx) contains native comments, replies and pending tracked changes generated from this same document.
HTML views and filters do not change what is exported.
Discussion Markdown currently retains its stored punctuation in Word rather than becoming native Word formatting.

To start from a reviewed Word document, import it into a new directory:

~~~sh
quarto-review import-docx reviewed.docx --into candidate --author "Your Name"
~~~

Import preserves supported review records and archives the original Word file.
Inspect a returned draft as a candidate alongside the version you sent; the single-source workflow does not automatically merge independently edited Word returns.
See the [format guide](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review/blob/main/docs/single-source.md) and [tested compatibility](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review/blob/main/docs/status.md) for details.

:::: {.review-thread #c1 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:01:00Z}
Could we say **modest** here?
The estimate does not support “large”.

- Keep the direction of the result.
- Qualify its magnitude.

::: {.reply #r1 by=A at=2026-09-01T10:00:00Z}
Agreed.
I have left the replacement pending so we can compare both versions.
:::
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c2 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:15:00Z}
Were the same word lists used in both sessions?

::: {.reply #r2 by=A at=2026-09-01T10:05:00Z}
No; each session used a different list.
:::

::: {.reply #r3 by=R at=2026-09-01T10:10:00Z to=r2}
Thanks.
Please include that distinction in the methods.
:::
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c3 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:20:00Z}
How long after the second practice session was the test?
My range overlaps Robin's, but this is a separate question about timing.
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c4 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:25:00Z .resolved}
Is this the planned or final sample?

::: {.reply #r4 by=A at=2026-09-01T10:15:00Z}
The planned sample; “recruitment target” makes that explicit.
:::
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c5 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:30:00Z}
Please include **all three**:

1. The estimated difference.
2. An uncertainty interval.
3. The analysed sample size.

Use `n` consistently for the sample size.
See [working locally](#work-locally) to reply to this discussion.
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c6 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:35:00Z format=plain}
Keep *asterisks*, _underscores_ and [brackets] exactly as written.
This synthetic message demonstrates the literal format used for imported Word text.
::::
